text.content:
Three peoples fight the same war with the same physics and opposite manners. A Soul Reaper carries their own soul as a sword, and it argues with them. A Hollow ate its own heart and wears the hole. A Quincy owns no soul-weapon at all — they reach into the air and make a bow out of what is already there.

Mechanically they are one chassis: 10 Hit Points, light armour, a Reiatsu DC, and a focus pool that refills by fighting.

The three things a new player should know

  • The pool is the spike; the Lineage is the floor. Every Lineage has a free, repeatable ranged option from 1st level with an empty pool — Shō, Bala, or Heizen.
  • Release is not a stance. It lasts the whole encounter, doesn't conflict with stance actions, and the first one each encounter is free.
  • Every technique costs exactly one Reiatsu Point. There is no 2-point effect anywhere in the class.

Your reiatsu pool is Pathfinder's focus pool: 1 point, 2 at 5th level, 3 at 11th. Steady the Breath is Refocus — you meditate, or you argue with your sword, or you eat something.

Rising Pressure

Once per round, the first time you either deal damage to an enemy with your spirit weapon or take damage from an enemy, you regain 1 Reiatsu Point. You can't exceed your maximum, and over a single encounter you can't regain more points this way than your maximum pool size.

That last clause is the one that matters. Without it a long fight is an infinite pool. The module enforces it and will say so in chat when a point is granted.

LevelPoolPer encounterTechniques per fight
1–41+12
5–102+24
11–203+36

A note for the GM

The pool's size is set from your level, not from how many techniques you happen to know. Pathfinder normally derives a focus pool from the effects you know, which would leave a Hollow — who knows exactly one costed kidō, forever — on a pool of one at 11th level. If someone "fixes" that, the Hollow and the Quincy quietly lose two thirds of their resource.

Four rungs, and each is a state rather than a stance.

RungLevelLasts
Release (Shikai / Resurrección / Schrift)1the encounter
Refined Release9—
Full Release (Bankai / Segunda Etapa / Vollständig)131 minute, 2 from 17th
Final Release — Severance2010 rounds, once per week

What the module does for you

Releasing applies the state and its effects; the encounter ending takes them away. A released form that replaces your weapon — Luz de la Luna, Gran Caída, Starrk's pistols — stows the sealed profile and hands it back when the form ends. Your runes stay on it.

At 20th level, Final Release puts you into Severance for ten rounds. Somewhere inside those ten rounds you get exactly one irreversible attack — your Severing Art — and it is worth less the longer you wait.

Round of SeveranceDiceAverage
1st20d670.0
2nd18d663.0
3rd16d656.0
4th14d649.0
5th12d642.0
6th10d635.0
7th8d628.0
8th, 9th, 10thcannot be used

Dice = 22 − 2 × the round number.

The tension is the point. Round one is 70 damage and none of the buff. Round seven is 28 damage and six rounds of a 4d6 rider, doubled Flash Step and free kidō. There is no dominant line.

Using the Art ends Severance whether you want it to or not, and when Severance ends by either route you lose your Released Form, your Release Technique, your Full Release and your entire pool until a week of downtime.

If your table finds everyone fires on round one, flatten the table — start at 16d6 and drop 1d6 a round — rather than cutting the ceiling. The module keeps this arithmetic in one function for exactly that reason.

Kidō are not spells. They use your Reiatsu DC, can't be counteracted as spells, and can't be heightened with slots. They auto-heighten to half your level, rounded up.

LineageFree cantripCostedChosen?
Soul ReaperShōsix, at 1st (×2), 5th, 9th, 13th, 17thchosen
HollowBalaone — Cerofixed
QuincyHeizenone — Gritzfixed

The ceilings are load-bearing. Additional Kidō is Soul Reaper only and takeable three times, so the hard ceiling is nine at 20th for a Soul Reaper who spends three class feats on it — and that character has given up three Zanjutsu techniques to do it. A Hollow or Quincy can never exceed two.

There is no utility kidō in the list. No flight, no invisibility, no teleport, no divination. Every entry is damage, control, a shield, or a small heal. The moment a Soul Reaper can solve arbitrary problems with magic, the class is a Magus with better hit points.

Ryūjin Jakka burns your own party

Zanka no Tachi deals 1d6 fire at the start of each of its user's turns to every creature within 30 feet including allies. That is deliberate and canon — Yamamoto's Bankai is a liability to everyone standing near it — and the module makes it actually happen rather than leaving it in prose.

If your table dislikes friendly fire, the cleanest fix is to exempt allies and reduce the die steps from two to one. That is a table decision; the default content does not make it for you.

Kyōka Suigetsu remembers

The hypnosis is keyed to what a creature has seen, not to the current fight. The module keeps a register per creature: whether it has seen a Shikai release, what it rolled, and which immunity window it is in. That memory outlives the encounter and travels between scenes, because canon's clause does.

The blind are immune entirely. That is Aizen's only blind spot and it is worth remembering when you build encounters against one.

What is invented

Nine of the fifteen Severing Arts are the character's actual canon technique. The other six are extrapolations built on a principle canon does establish, and each says so at the top of its own description. Several Segunda Etapas and Kyōka Suigetsu's Bankai are likewise invented — Ulquiorra is explicitly the only Espada who reached a Segunda Etapa, and Aizen has no Bankai. Nothing is presented as something the manga contains.

Reactions

Eight abilities trigger on someone else's action. When one is available the module whispers the owner a card with a single button. Ignoring the card declines the reaction — nothing is spent, and nobody's turn is held up waiting.
